content: Common forgotten details running untrusted Python via subprocess: killing only the parent leaves zombies until something calls wait()/join() on it - zombies accumulate and can hit the OS per-user PID limit; must always reap (process.join() or Popen.wait()) after kill; fork bombs are trivial in unrestricted Python (os.fork() loop) so RLIMIT_NPROC is required; a runaway process's own grandchildren survive parent kill unless launched in their own process group and killed via killpg.
